notes:
[TXT027-order] Manuscript page 26 says refinement and subdivision determine each other given the subfigure order. It asks “Peut-on de = exprimer ≤ en termes de ≪ et de ≼ ?”; the margin contains “??”.

[TXT027-NB] The NB states F≤G and F≼G imply F=G. The next sentence is “Il faudra que ceci soit vrai”, with toute cancelled before contrée. The argument posits a nonempty H disjoint from F refining G when F<G; C5 would then transfer disjointness from F to G, leading to H empty. The existence assertion for H is not proved here. The readers checked this conditional reduction only, with the factorization and interpretation of disjointness as assumptions. The handwritten gloss says H comp. à G; H’s raffine changes its meaning and is rejected on the visible c-o-m-p abbreviation.

[TXT027-axioms] C5 is called trivial and justified by equal supports; the set-theoretic equality-of-intersections step was checked. C6 says “on la verra tantôt”. C7 says “on le vérifiera” with an unresolved contracted ending; the isolated enlargement favours tautologiq^t / topologiq^t but does not exclude de tte façon. The final label is not secure as plain C8: it has a distinct low zero. The cancelled heading reads Famille intersection(s). No date, title sheet, or page-count statement is present; handwritten page number 26.

Checked only the set-theoretic step: if |H|⊆|G| and |H|∩|G|=∅, then |H|=∅. Thus the middle implication is coherent under the figure/support identifications used by the page. No full axiom-system proof claimed.
